transcript.text: Shark NV602UK has lost loads of suction and whistles. Found a split in the flexible hose near the handle end. Is it the hose I need?

Yes, a split hose is almost certainly your main problem. On the NV602UK (Lift-Away upright), the flexible hose carries all the airflow from the floor head to the dust cup. A split lets air leak in, so you lose suction at the floor head, and the air rushing through the gap causes the whistle. The handle end is a very common place for it to fail, because it flexes most there.

**Quick test before buying:** Wrap the split tightly with electrical or duct tape and run the vacuum. If the whistle stops and suction mostly comes back, the hose is the fault.

**Replacing it:**
- Buy a hose listed for the **NV602UK** (or a compatible NV600/NV601/NV602 Lift-Away hose). Shark UK sells genuine spares, and there are cheaper third-party versions on Amazon and eBay. Check the listing matches your model and includes the handle-end fitting if your split is near it.
- Fitting is usually tool-free or needs just a screwdriver. The hose clips or screws in at the handle end and the lower pod end.

**Check these too while you're at it,** since lost suction often has more than one cause:
- **Filters:** Wash the foam and felt pre-motor filters under the dust cup in cold water only, and let them dry for at least 24 hours. Tap out or rinse the post-motor HEPA filter behind the front grille.
- **Blockages:** Look through the hose, the wand, the inlet at the bottom of the dust cup, and the neck of the floor head.
- **Brushroll:** Cut away any hair wrapped around it.
- **Seals:** Make sure the dust cup is seated properly and its seals aren't cracked.

If you tape the split and it still whistles, look for a second crack or a loose connection at either end of the hose.
Covering the split with my hand makes suction much better, and I've temporarily taped it. Do I need just the hose or the hose with the handle assembly?

Usually **just the hose**, but check how yours attaches before ordering.

**Look at where the hose meets the handle:**
- **Separate fitting:** If there's a cuff or collar that clips, twists, or screws into the handle, and the handle plastic itself isn't damaged, you only need the hose. Most NV60x replacement hoses come with the end fittings already attached.
- **Bonded fitting:** If the hose looks permanently glued or moulded into the handle, with no way to separate them, you'll need the hose-with-handle assembly.
- **Cracked handle:** If the split runs into the handle plastic or the hose's end fitting, rather than just the ribbed flexible section, get the assembly or a hose that includes that fitting.

**When ordering:**
- Compare the photo with your vacuum, especially both end fittings.
- Check whether the listing says "hose only" or "with handle."
- Search by your model number (**NV602UK**) rather than a generic "Shark hose." Some similar-looking Lift-Away hoses have slightly different ends.

If you can't tell how it comes apart, Shark UK customer service can confirm the right part number for your model and the serial number on the sticker under the dust cup.

The tape will hold in the meantime. Just keep an eye on it, because the split can grow with flexing.
Not sure how it attaches, the split is just in the ribbed bit by the cuff at the handle end. I don't know if the cuff comes off. Is hose only fine then?

Very likely yes. The damage is in the flexible hose itself, not the handle, so a replacement hose will fix it. The only catch is that the new hose has to be able to connect to your handle.

**The safe way to order:**
- Pick a hose listed for the **NV602UK** whose photo shows a cuff or fitting on **both ends**, matching yours.
- Then you'll be replacing the whole hose, cuff included, so it doesn't matter whether your old cuff comes off separately.

**To see how yours comes apart before it arrives:**
- Look around the handle end for small screws, often under the handle or near the cuff.
- Look for a release button or tab, or try a firm twist-and-pull on the cuff.
- Don't force it. If nothing gives, wait for the new hose, which may come with fitting instructions, or search YouTube for "Shark NV602 hose replacement" to see it done.

If the handle turns out to be one piece with the hose, you'd need the assembly instead. Order from a seller with easy returns, or ask Shark UK, so you can swap it if it doesn't match.
